meta.title: Session J decision record
meta.basis: Six strategies scored on a seeded 10,000-trial certainty equivalent at CRRA = 2, per $100,000 of in-place NOI, carried to 2040. Engine: scripts/model.py. Ranking and all figures are regenerated by that script; this file holds the decision narrative, the phased plan and the triggers, not the arithmetic.

recommendation.headline: Dual track: secure term, then sell into it.
recommendation.detail: Approach the tenant in 2026 for a 10-15 year extension at or above in-place rent. In parallel, engage a qualified intermediary and identify replacement property. Sell in 2029-2032 with more than ten years of term, through a Section 1031 exchange into a diversified net-lease portfolio. If the extension fails at acceptable rent, sell in 2028. If tenant credit cracks, sell immediately. Hold for income beyond 2032 only if the owner is comfortable keeping a single building in an earthquake zone on its own balance sheet.
recommendation.what_this_preserves: Wealth preservation: it avoids the two documented value leaks in this analysis - term decay and paying tax that a qualified exchange can defer. Growth: the owner keeps the rent stream through the extension period and enters a diversified portfolio at the sale. Manageable risk: it exits single-site, single-tenant concentration within six years rather than holding it indefinitely.
recommendation.confidence: High on the direction (do not hold passively to expiry; defer tax via 1031; do not let the lease expire), moderate on the timing (2029-2032 versus 2036 is a liquidity preference, not an arithmetic one, because the top three strategies are within about 6% of each other on the risk-adjusted measure).

plan.what: Read the lease; confirm the exact expiry, options, notice dates, guaranty, assignment clause and insurance responsibilities. Obtain franchisee financials and unit-level sales.
plan.why: Every number in this workbook is normalised because these facts were not supplied. They change the answer more than any market forecast.

plan.what: Approach the tenant and the brand for a 10-15 year extension or at or above in-place rent, with escalations at or above CPI.
plan.why: Term is the value driver, and an extension costs no transaction tax.

plan.what: Commission a broker opinion of value and, if a sale is likely, a Phase I environmental site assessment and a seismic review.
plan.why: The cap rate is the single largest assumption in the model and there is no official cap-rate series. This is the only way to replace an assumption with evidence.

plan.what: Decision gate: extension signed at acceptable rent? Yes: prepare a 2029-2031 sale. No: list in 2028.
Sell through a qualified intermediary with 12+ years of term; identify replacement properties within 45 days and close within 180.
plan.why: Capture the term premium and defer the tax.

plan.what: Re-run this model with the new Treasury curve, the tenant's latest 10-Q, and a fresh insurance quote.
plan.why: The triggers are quantitative so they can be tested rather than argued about.

triggers.trigger: No extension at or above in-place rent by 31 December 2027
triggers.action: Sell in 2028 through a Section 1031 exchange
triggers.reason: Without term the asset is already in the decay zone; the model's extend-then-sell case collapses towards the sell-now case.

triggers.trigger: Missed rent, a franchisee bankruptcy filing, or the unit appears on a brand closure list
triggers.action: Sell immediately; do not wait for the extension
triggers.reason: Every modelled no-renewal path is materially worse than selling with term in place.

triggers.action: Bring the sale forward into the cap-rate compression
triggers.reason: A 50 bp cap-rate move is worth about $310,000 per $100,000 of NOI in this model.

triggers.action: Do not sell into the spike; hold income and revisit in two quarters
triggers.reason: Selling into a rate spike converts a temporary discount into a permanent loss.

triggers.trigger: Renewal offer more than 10% below in-place rent
triggers.action: Reject the renewal and sell with the remaining term
triggers.reason: The model's 10% rent-cut case destroys about $424,000 of terminal wealth.

triggers.trigger: Insurance premium more than doubles, or earthquake cover is withdrawn
triggers.reason: The owner cannot transfer an uninsurable risk; diversification reduces single-site exposure.

triggers.trigger: Measure ULA indexation pushes the sale price across the $5.4m threshold
triggers.action: Re-price and take structuring advice before listing
triggers.reason: The 4.0% surtax applies to the whole consideration, not just the excess over the threshold.

what_would_change_the_answer.factor: A corporate guaranty or letter of credit
what_would_change_the_answer.effect: Materially lowers credit risk and pushes the recommendation towards holding for income.

what_would_change_the_answer.factor: In-place rent below market with a fixed-price tenant option
what_would_change_the_answer.effect: The renewal option becomes a landlord liability; the calculus inverts towards selling before the option is exercised.

what_would_change_the_answer.factor: A very low basis and no appetite to reinvest
what_would_change_the_answer.effect: A sale becomes a tax event with no offsetting benefit; the hold case improves by roughly the 646,520 difference between S01 and S02 per $100,000 of NOI.

what_would_change_the_answer.factor: Redevelopment value exceeding the net-lease value
what_would_change_the_answer.effect: None of this analysis applies; the question becomes a land residual, which this workbook does not attempt.
